title: Add missing translations for verse selection effects options
summary: In a shared session, the **Verse Selection Effects** setting has three buttons. Before this change they showed raw code names like `session-settings-verse-effects-hosts-only` instead of words; now they read **Hosts only**, **Everyone** and **None**. The flash on a verse number when someone selects a verse also now lasts about 3 seconds instead of about 1 second, so it's easier to notice.

setup.title: Get two browsers side by side
setup.body: The tests need two people in the same session. Use two different browsers on a computer (for example Chrome and Firefox), or one normal window and one private/incognito window (Ctrl+Shift+N in Chrome/Edge, Ctrl+Shift+P in Firefox; on Mac use Cmd instead of Ctrl). Place them side by side so you can watch both at once. Below they're called the **host browser** and the **guest browser**.

setup.title: Open the preview build in both
setup.body: Open the preview link at the top of this page in both browsers. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like an older version of Seed Bible, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in with two different accounts
setup.body: Sign in in each browser with a **different** email address. Seed Bible emails you a code to type in, so use two inboxes you can check.

setup.title: Start a shared session
setup.body: In the host browser, open **John 3**. Click the **Share** button (the share icon at the top of the tabs side bar), then **Start and share session**. You'll see "A link to join the shared session was copied to your clipboard". Paste that link into the guest browser's address bar and open it. Both browsers should now show John 3 in a shared session, with both people listed as participants.

setup.title: Open Session settings
setup.body: In the host browser, open the shared tab's menu (the **⋮** / **Tab options** button on the tab) and choose **Session settings**. Scroll to the **Verse Selection Effects** section, below **Highlight for**.

sections.title: The setting's buttons have readable names

tests.title: The three buttons show words, not code names
tests.why: This is the main fix. Before, the buttons showed text like `session-settings-verse-effects-hosts-only`.
steps: Look at the buttons in the **Verse Selection Effects** section.
expected: There are three buttons reading **Hosts only**, **Everyone** and **None**, in that order.
No button shows a long hyphenated code name like `session-settings-verse-effects-…`.
In a new session, **Hosts only** is shown as selected.

tests.title: Clicking each button selects it and updates the description
expected: After **Everyone**: that button looks selected and the line under the buttons reads "Show effects when anyone selects a verse."
After **None**: that button looks selected and the line reads "Verse selection effects are turned off for everyone."
After **Hosts only**: that button looks selected and the line reads "Show effects when a host selects a verse."
Button labels stay the same words throughout.

tests.title: Buttons stay readable on a phone-width screen
steps: Make the host browser window very narrow (about the width of a phone), or open the session on a phone.
Open **Session settings** again and scroll to **Verse Selection Effects**.
expected: All three button labels are fully readable: not cut off, overlapping, or spilling outside the dialog.

tests.title: In another language, the buttons still show words
tests.why: Only the English wording was added; translators fill in other languages later. Until then the buttons should fall back to English words rather than code names.
steps: In the host browser, open Seed Bible's **Settings** and change **Language** to another language (for example Español).
Open the shared tab's menu, choose the session settings item, and find the verse selection effects section.
Change the language back to English afterwards.
expected: The three buttons show words (in English is fine), never a code name like `session-settings-verse-effects-…`.

sections.title: The verse number flash lasts longer
sections.intro: When someone selects a verse, the small verse number in front of it lights up in that person's color for the **other** people in the session, then fades out.

tests.title: With Hosts only, the host's selection flashes for about 3 seconds
tests.before: In Session settings, **Hosts only** is selected. Close the dialog and keep both browsers on John 3.
steps: In the host browser, click **John 3:16** to select it.
Watch verse number 16 in the guest browser and count roughly how long the glow lasts.
expected: In the guest browser, the number **16** lights up in the host's color and fades back to normal over about **3 seconds** (before this change it was about 1 second).
The host browser's own verse number does not flash.

tests.title: With Hosts only, the guest's selection does not flash
steps: Watch verse number 17 in the host browser.
expected: Verse number 17 does not flash in the host browser.

tests.title: With Everyone, the guest's selection flashes for about 3 seconds
tests.before: In the host browser, open **Session settings**, choose **Everyone**, and close the dialog.
steps: Watch verse number 17 in the host browser.
expected: In the host browser, the number **17** lights up in the guest's color and fades out over about 3 seconds.

tests.title: Selecting verses quickly in a row still flashes each one
tests.why: With the longer flash, a new selection could start while the last one is still fading.
steps: In the host browser, click **John 3:16**, then within a second click **John 3:17**, then click **John 3:16** again.
expected: Each click makes the selected verse's number flash in the guest browser, including the second click on 16.
No verse number is left stuck glowing after about 3 seconds have passed since the last click.

tests.title: With None, nothing flashes
tests.before: In the host browser, open **Session settings**, choose **None**, and close the dialog.
expected: No verse number flashes in either browser.

notCovered: Translations into languages other than English. Only the English wording was added; translators handle the rest.
